posts.title: Teuchi Ren Ramen: Hand-Made Noodles in Morishita
posts.description: The shio broth uses five selected salts with dried shiitake and Hokkaido scallop, including dried scallop adductor. There's no chemical seasoning in it, and it's impressive that a shop can build this much flavor from ingredients alone.

posts.title: The Best Umeda Ramen: Bowls Worth Walking For in Osaka
posts.description: If you only have time for one bowl in Umeda, this is the one. Mugi to Mensuke builds its soup on guinea fowl, which gives the shoyu a wilder, more assertive flavor than your typical tanrei (delicate) bowl.

posts.title: Toen: The Tamana Ramen Shop Behind Kumamoto Tonkotsu
posts.description: Like a lot of Kumamoto-area ramen, the soup here is 100% pork. Pork leg bones and backbones go into a big hagama pot over a high-powered kerosene burner and get boiled hard, the same way the founder did it.
